You’re sat on a peaceful residential street halfway between Francis Road and Coronation Gardens here, with both charming cafes and landscaped greenery at your fingertips. Sidmouth Park is also just one street over, and the speedy Central line links of Leyton tube are ten minutes on foot.
Your new home

You have a dedicated front door and modest entrance hall. Climb the stairs to immediately arrive on a proper landing with the extensive open plan kitchen and living room to the rear. We’ll explore there shortly.

Your principal bedroom sits to the front, a magnificent double of more than 150 square feet, full of natural light from the large bay window and secondary sash, both dressed flawlessly in classic bistro shutters. A tower radiator, integrated wardrobe and tranquil mint green colour scheme complete the effect.

Back to the rear, and your open plan kitchen, diner and reception space is over twenty seven feet deep, with blonde parquet flooring, exposed brick and a striking mix of pristine white and warm coral paintwork combining to dramatic effect.

Twin skylights are set into the high, vaulted ceiling, with dual aspect windows adding to the floods of natural light. The kitchen area is artfully zoned towards the front, with sleek and seamless glossy cabinetry and chunky white worktops sat against the exposed brick. A superb space that elevates the everyday.

Step out at the rear for a sizeable timber deck and rooftop views, perfect for morning coffee or an evening glass of wine. Stairs descend to your private south facing garden ; a pristine patio leading to a lush lawn, flanked by high, dark timber fencing. A nicely secluded outdoor retreat.

Back inside, and your family bathroom completes the first floor; tiled from floor to ceiling in large format white letterboxes, with a classic white suite and hardwood style vinyl underfoot.

Finally, head upstairs - that lovely exposed brickwork climbing with you - for the gloriously skylit loft suite. There’s around 180 square feet up here, finished with inset shelving and white walls, all flooded with natural light and with an absolute wealth of extra storage under the eaves. Always a welcome bonus in London apartment living. A suitably striking final space in a superb duplex.

Francis Road, less than five minutes away, has remained Leyton’s most sought-after social hub even as the surrounding area goes from strength to strength, with an ever increasing range of cafes, drinking spots and eating out.

Albert & Francis is still the favoured coffee spot, with expert artisanal brews. Yardarm offers a carefully curated range of wines to enjoy inside or take away, while Marmelo Kitchen has deli delicacies for your larder.

Also be sure to check out the kerb street market, every Saturday. Great for fresh produce.

Just as close in the other direction is Leyton High Road, home to a range of pubs and bars including E10’s premier gastropub; The Leyton Engineer, sat in the Grade II listed surroundings of the Old Town Hall.

As noted, you have the green spaces of Coronation Gardens and Sidmouth Park on your doorstep, and if you really want to stretch your legs, Leyton Jubilee Park and even Hackney Marshes are within reach, for a genuine city escape.

Finally, Leyton tube connects you to the heart of the capital via the Central line. Just ten minutes on foot from your new front door, from here you can be at Liverpool Street in ten minutes, or Oxford Circus in twenty.

The Home -

Behind a handsome London-stock-brick façade, this characterful Victorian home pairs original period detail with a simple, pared-back interior and a private garden to the rear.

The house retains much of what gives homes of this era their appeal: Deep bay windows, stripped timber floorboards, decorative fireplaces and high ceilings. A restrained palette of white walls allows these original elements to do much of the talking, while the open-plan kitchen and dining space at the rear brings a more relaxed, contemporary feel.

Albert Road sits particularly close to Francis Road, one of Leyton's best-loved neighbourhood streets, known for its independent shops, cafés and places to eat.

The Indoors

The front bedroom is wonderfully evocative of the house's Victorian origins. A broad bay window draws in plenty of natural light, while stripped floorboards run underfoot. The original fireplace is particularly lovely, with an ornate cast-iron surround, green glazed tiles and a graphic tiled hearth providing a focal point to the otherwise understated room.

Further along, a second bedroom room continues the same material language, with timber boards and another cast-iron fireplace. Its proportions lend themselves easily to use as a bedroom, study or quieter living space depending on need.

At the rear, the kitchen and dining room have been opened into one sociable space. White cabinetry sits beneath timber worktops, with classic metro tiles lining the splashback and a simple peninsula subtly defining the kitchen. Windows to both sides bring light into the room, while a glazed door provides a direct connection to the garden.

There is a pleasing continuity throughout the house, with the dark original floorboards contrasting against crisp white walls and joinery. The bathroom is similarly straightforward, combining white wall tiles with a small-scale monochrome mosaic floor.

The Outdoors

The kitchen opens directly onto a private rear garden, beginning with a useful paved side return before extending into a longer lawned garden.

Mature planting and established boundaries give the space a pleasing sense of enclosure, while a raised brick-edged seating area at the far end creates a natural spot for outdoor dining. There is plenty of opportunity here for someone to develop the planting further and make the garden their own.

Loving The Location

Albert Road occupies a particularly appealing pocket of Leyton, with the independent shops and cafés of Francis Road close at hand. The partly pedestrianised street has become a genuine neighbourhood hub and is home to Yardarm for wine, bread and provisions, Marmelo General Store and Tamping Grounds for coffee.

Leyton and Leytonstone provide a wider selection of shops and everyday amenities, while the area's transport connections include Leyton on the Central line and Leyton Midland Road on the Suffragette line.

The wider neighbourhood also puts some of east London's best green spaces within easy reach, with the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park to the south and the open spaces around Hackney Marshes and the Lea Valley beyond.
